correctness.rationale: Conditional source/path counting gives exact joint and marginal probabilities. AM-GM proves strict endpoint negativity. One-closed-edge expansion proves the precise high-p sign coefficient, and p=0 gives negative baseline. Integer CDF counts give strictly positive nonconstant coefficients of F_n/(1-p), yielding a unique boundary-adjacent root and its asymptotics. Full finite enumeration in check.py passed 20,483 exact rational assertions, but the unrestricted proof is analytical.

originality.rationale: Exact uniform-random-source path covariance classification, endpoint-only perpetual anticorrelation, and the unique endpoint-adjacent threshold were compared with relevant literature searches and inspected full-text scientific sources. The general epidemic-percolation and tree-equation frameworks do not state the claimed sign geometry; fixed-root association is not the unconditional random-root covariance; finite-time infectious-state correlation is a different observable. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: The 2014 Cator/Van Mieghem article full text was not obtained; its abstract and the full 2018 comment indicate different state/time observables.
A combinatorially equivalent random-root percolation or path-reliability result might exist under an unsearched title; lack of search hits is not a proof of novelty.
The analysis is limited to independent undirected bonds; arbitrary Markovian SIR infectious-period dependence is outside scope.

value.rationale: The precise dependence of final infection indicators can change sign depending on contact-position geometry even under homogeneous independent transmission and one shared outbreak source. The endpoint-only permanent anticorrelation, all-other-pairs high-transmission positivity, and exact inverse-path-length boundary-pair transition give nontrivial analytic benchmarks for network surveillance covariance modeling and dependence interpretation, not merely a single numerical example.
